title: wksplit-cs-utility: C#/PS splitter with 6-gate safety
desc: Auto-split large .cs/.ps1 files into partial classes or modules. 6 mandatory gates prevent parse-clean-but-dead splits. SPLIT-FIRST: run this before deep-reading or refactoring any >400-line source -- it is free, deterministic, and leaves the code better than you found it. Howto: wksplit-cs-utility-howto. Incidents/history: wksplit-cs-utility-ref.
steps: PURPOSE: wksplit-cs splits large .cs files into C# partial classes; wksplit-ps1 splits .ps1 into dot-sourced modules. Both run 6 mandatory safety gates and exit only on a verified-clean result. Use: python bin/wksplit-cs.py <file.cs> [-m <max-lines>] or bin/wksplit-ps1.ps1 <file.ps1>.

GATE 1 -- PARAM-FIRST: param() block stays the FIRST statement in every PS1 output file; all dot-sourcing/module imports placed strictly below it. Violation silently parses clean and only dies at runtime. Detail + history: [[wksplit-cs-utility-ref]].

GATE 2 -- REGEX-HOIST: every inline regex literal containing non-ASCII chars is replaced with a :<Name>Rx var placed after param(). Prevents encoding corruption across bash->PowerShell relay. Implementation detail (PS 5.1 scriptblock scope trap, verified pattern): [[wksplit-cs-utility-howto]].

GATE 3 -- SYMBOL-REFERENCE PRE-CHECK: collect all FunctionDefinitionAst names across all planned modules; compare to all CommandAst.GetCommandName() calls. Any function called in the original but missing from the planned output is a DROPPED function -> auto-remerge or FAIL. This is the gate that would have saved wkhippo.

GATE 4 -- RUN-VERIFY (PS) / COMPILE-UNTIL-CLEAN (C#): PS: actually run the split tool once on a real input -- a clean parse is NOT proof (see G1/G3). C#: run dotnet build in a loop, auto-remerge any member causing CS0103/CS0246, retry until 0 warnings AND 0 errors. Exit only on clean build.

GATE 5 -- RECOMBINE: emit a recombine artifact (-main.ps1 or wksplit -Recombine mode) that dot-sources/concatenates modules back to the original monolith. Proves round-trip correctness and is the instant recovery path if a deployed split breaks.
GATE 6 -- SELFTEST: built-in self-test creates a temp .csproj, copies split partials (original renamed .bak to avoid CS0111 duplicates), compiles, verifies. Run with --selftest flag.

SPLIT-FIRST ANALYSIS: any source >400 lines or hard to reason about -> split FIRST, then analyze the small focused modules. The split is FREE (zero tokens, pure AST/build), SAFE (G4/G6 guarantee no broken split ships), and leaves the code under the ~400-line cap. [[wksplit-cs-utility-howto]] [[wksplit-cs-utility-ref]]
